definitions.explanation: The office procedure of submitting receipts for money spent on company business and being paid back for it. A routine monthly task in Japanese workplaces.

examples.japanese: {経費精算|けいひせいさん}を{忘|わす}れていた。
examples.english: I forgot to file my expense claim.

examples.japanese: {出張|しゅっちょう}の{領収書|りょうしゅうしょ}をまとめて{経費精算|けいひせいさん}した。
examples.english: I gathered the receipts from my business trip and filed the expense claim.

examples.japanese: {経費精算|けいひせいさん}の{締|し}め{切|き}りは{毎月|まいつき}{五日|いつか}です。
examples.english: The deadline for expense claims is the fifth of every month.

examples.japanese: {紙|かみ}の{申請書|しんせいしょ}をやめてから、{経費精算|けいひせいさん}がずいぶん{楽|らく}になった。
examples.english: Since we stopped using paper forms, expense reimbursement has become much easier.

notes:
Formed from {経費|けいひ} (business expenses) + {精算|せいさん} (settling up). Takes する. Note the kanji: {精算|せいさん} means settling an amount exactly, while the homophone {清算|せいさん} means liquidating or winding up.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {経費精算|けいひせいさん}をする: to file an expense claim
- {経費精算|けいひせいさん}システム: expense reimbursement system
- {経費|けいひ}で{落|お}とす: to put something on the company's expenses

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {立替|たてか}え: paying on someone's behalf — the outlay that the reimbursement repays
- {仮払|かりばら}い: cash advance — money paid out before the expense is incurred
- {領収書|りょうしゅうしょ}: receipt — the document a claim normally requires
